title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court and the China Insurance Regulatory Commission on Carrying Out Pilot Work in Some Regions of the Country for Establishing a Linkage Mechanism between Litigation and Mediation for Insurance Disputes
keywords_en: Carrying out the establishment of insurance dispute resolution in some regions
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court, China Insurance Regulatory Commission

Notice on Carrying Out Pilot Work on Establishing a Mechanism for Linking Litigation and Mediation in Insurance Disputes in Selected Regions Nationwide

[2012] No. 307

Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; all insurance regulatory bureaus; all insurance industry associations:

In order to implement the central authorities' overall plan for reforming the connection mechanism between litigation and non-litigation dispute resolution, and the people's courts' working principle of "mediation first, combining mediation with adjudication," and to fully leverage the positive role of insurance regulatory authorities and insurance industry organizations in preventing and resolving social disputes, and to resolve insurance disputes in a lawful, fair, and efficient manner, the Supreme People's Court and the China Insurance Regulatory Commission have decided to jointly carry out pilot work on establishing a mechanism for linking litigation and mediation in insurance disputes in selected regions nationwide (the list of pilot regions is attached). The relevant matters are hereby notified as follows:

I. Work Objectives

1. To establish and improve a diversified dispute resolution mechanism for insurance disputes, promote lawful, fair, efficient, and proper resolution of conflicts and disputes, provide parties to insurance disputes with more alternative dispute resolution channels, safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of all parties, and promote the sustained and healthy development of the insurance industry.

II. Work Principles

2. Principle of Lawfulness and Fairness. The work of linking litigation and mediation in insurance disputes shall be conducted lawfully and fairly, strictly following the procedures stipulated by laws, administrative regulations, and judicial interpretations, fully respecting the parties' intentions, and no compulsory mediation shall be allowed; relevant mediation work shall not harm the legitimate rights and interests of the parties or interested parties, shall not violate the basic principles of law, and shall not harm the public interest.

3. Principle of Efficiency and Convenience. In carrying out the work of linking litigation and mediation in insurance disputes, attention shall be paid to work efficiency; mediation shall not be delayed by stalling, and cases shall not be mediated for a long time without resolution; the form, time, and place of mediation shall be flexibly determined according to the actual circumstances of the dispute, so as to facilitate the parties as much as possible and reduce their costs of dispute resolution.

4. Principle of Active and Prudent Approach. The establishment of a mechanism for linking litigation and mediation in insurance disputes is to be carried out by first piloting and then promoting. Courts and insurance regulatory authorities in pilot regions shall actively explore, prudently advance, carefully summarize and accumulate experience, and gradually promote it to other regions nationwide when conditions mature.

III. Work Requirements

5. Courts and insurance regulatory authorities in pilot regions shall fully recognize the importance of this work, strengthen organizational leadership, establish and improve systems, and continuously enhance the fairness and credibility of the work of linking litigation and mediation in insurance disputes.

6. Courts in pilot regions may, in accordance with the spirit of the Supreme People's Court's "Overall Plan for Expanding the Pilot Reform of the Dispute Resolution Mechanism Linking Litigation and Non-Litigation" (Fa [2012] No. 116), establish a roster of specially invited mediation organizations and a roster of specially invited mediators. They shall improve the management system for the rosters, provide complete and accurate information on mediation organizations and mediators to parties in insurance disputes for their voluntary choice. They shall make full use of the court's litigation and mediation linkage work platform. Courts with the necessary conditions may also provide mediation rooms dedicated to handling insurance disputes for specially invited mediation organizations and mediators to carry out their work.

7. Insurance regulatory authorities shall strengthen guidance to insurance industry mediation organizations and supervise their standardized operation. They shall guide local insurance industry associations to establish industry mediation organizations and specify the funding sources for mediation organizations, assist insurance industry mediation organizations in establishing and improving mediator selection systems, and provide stable funding and personnel support for mediation.

8. Insurance industry associations shall be responsible for the construction and operational management of insurance industry mediation organizations, improve work systems and procedures, formulate mediator work rules and codes of professional ethics, strengthen the training of mediators, continuously improve the professional quality and mediation skills of mediators, and promote the lawful and fair conduct of mediation work.

9. Courts in pilot regions shall, while respecting the parties' intentions, and in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Supreme People's Court's "Several Opinions on Establishing and Improving the Dispute Resolution Mechanism Linking Litigation and Non-Litigation" (Fa Fa [2009] No. 45), adopt methods such as referring to mediation before case filing or entrusting mediation after case filing, to guide parties to resolve disputes efficiently and at low cost through the mechanism for linking litigation and mediation in insurance disputes.

10. Insurance regulatory authorities shall guide insurance companies to actively handle conflicts and disputes through the mechanism for linking litigation and mediation in insurance disputes, and urge them to actively perform mediation and settlement agreements.

11. In accordance with the relevant provisions of the Supreme People's Court's "Several Opinions on Establishing and Improving the Dispute Resolution Mechanism Linking Litigation and Non-Litigation" (Fa Fa [2009] No. 45), the Supreme People's Court's "Overall Plan for Expanding the Pilot Reform of the Dispute Resolution Mechanism Linking Litigation and Non-Litigation" (Fa [2012] No. 116), and the Civil Procedure Law, a mediation agreement reached by parties to an insurance dispute through mediation conducted by a mediation organization or mediator has the nature of a civil contract. After being signed and sealed by the mediator and the mediation organization, the parties may apply to a people's court with jurisdiction to confirm its validity. A mediation agreement confirmed as valid by a people's court has the force of compulsory execution.

12. Courts and insurance regulatory authorities and insurance industry associations in pilot regions shall, through various channels, increase publicity for the mechanism linking litigation and mediation in insurance disputes, and enhance public understanding and awareness of this dispute resolution mechanism.

13. Courts and insurance regulatory authorities in pilot regions shall strengthen cooperation and exchanges, establish communication links and information sharing mechanisms, designate contact departments and contact persons, and promptly consult on issues encountered in the work of linking litigation and mediation in insurance disputes, so as to improve mediation quality and efficiency.

14. The Second Civil Division of the Supreme People's Court and the Insurance Consumer Rights Protection Bureau of the China Insurance Regulatory Commission shall be specifically responsible for guiding the pilot work. The higher people's courts or intermediate people's courts in the jurisdictions where the pilot region courts are located shall guide, supervise, and inspect the pilot work within their jurisdictions, and pay attention to summarizing pilot experiences to ensure the smooth progress of the pilot work. Issues encountered by courts and insurance regulatory authorities in pilot regions during the pilot work shall be reported promptly to the Supreme People's Court and the China Insurance Regulatory Commission.

15. People's courts, insurance regulatory authorities, and insurance industry associations in non-pilot regions may actively explore diversified resolution methods for insurance disputes, draw on the successful experiences of pilot regions, and lay a good foundation for the establishment and improvement of a mechanism for linking litigation and mediation in insurance disputes.
